steps: Healthy member emits heartbeats with identity and progress.
Monitor records arrival intervals rather than assuming perfect clocks.
Late arrivals increase suspicion under a chosen threshold.
Membership retains, probes, or evicts the member while accepting false suspicion risk.

lesson.scenario: A service discovery system uses periodic heartbeats, arrival history, and an active probe before removing an API instance from routing.
entities: Emits identity, epoch, and progress every two seconds
Persists last-seen time and consecutive misses
Computes suspicion from elapsed time and miss threshold
Checks whether the process is reachable
Publishes healthy instances to request routers
Stops selecting instances removed from membership
connections: evaluate elapsed time and missed intervals

steps.title: Healthy baseline
steps.narration: Instance 7 reports every two seconds and remains eligible for requests.
steps.outcome: A recent heartbeat is evidence that the process was alive when it sent the report.
steps.invariant: A heartbeat proves recent progress, not future availability.

steps.title: First interval missed
steps.narration: No report arrives at 10:00:06, so the detector records delay without changing membership.
steps.outcome: The service remains routable during the configured grace period.
steps.invariant: One late heartbeat is not proof of failure in an asynchronous network.

steps.title: Suspicion threshold reached
steps.narration: Three intervals pass without a heartbeat, so the detector marks the instance suspect.
steps.outcome: Suspicion triggers corroboration before the control plane removes capacity.
steps.invariant: Detection thresholds trade recovery speed for false-positive risk.

steps.title: Probe also times out
steps.narration: The active probe cannot reach instance 7 before its deadline.
steps.outcome: Missing passive evidence is corroborated by a failed active check.
steps.invariant: Failure detectors produce suspicion; they cannot prove why a process is unreachable.

steps.title: Membership and routing update
steps.narration: The registry publishes epoch 88 and routers stop sending new requests to instance 7.
steps.outcome: New traffic avoids the suspected instance.
steps.invariant: Routers consume a versioned membership update rather than infer health independently.

steps.title: Restart rejoins safely
steps.narration: The process restarts with epoch 13, proves readiness, and is admitted as a new incarnation.
steps.outcome: The replacement incarnation rejoins without reviving stale epoch-12 authority.
steps.invariant: Process epochs prevent delayed heartbeats from restoring stale membership.
